items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: Remember, in 1955, April 24, 1955, Emmett Till went to Sumner, Mississippi, came from Chicago, and so they claimed he winked at a white woman... They took Emmett Till out one night, and they lynched him.

ctx.x: Well, let's see what we can do. But my point was, why is this all coming, why are blacks becoming, why is it becoming relevant now? I mean, in 1950, and that wasn't happening in 1940 or 1930. Why at that time period?

Well, at that time you were beginning to see a change in the political structure of the state and of the nation. Remember, you had, like I said earlier, you had the White Citizen Council. Then you had the Ku Klux Klan with threats. In 1955, 54, 55, here comes Martin Luther King. All right, so he made a lot of white people mad. But you've got to remember, in 1955, April 24, 1955, Emmett Till went to Sumner, Mississippi, came from Chicago, and so they claimed he winked at a white woman. He was only 14 years of age,…
Okay, reel number three with Tech Stevens, August 29, 1995. Okay. Yeah, well you...
